The Miss International organisation announced her continental title on Thursday, November 26, following the grand finale held on Wednesday, November 25, which featured 73 contestants from different countries. Bolarinde, popularly known as Queen Dammy, secured a place among the Top 20 finalists before emerging as the African continental titleholder, although she did not advance to the Top 10. Reacting to her experience, the model had earlier shared an emotional message on Instagram, expressing excitement about reaching the final stage of the competition. “Some moments are too powerful to be just dreams; this is destiny calling!” she wrote. She added that the experience felt like standing at the threshold of something extraordinary, with faith and hope. Bolarinde earned the right to represent Nigeria after winning the Face of Hope 2026 pageant at the Eko Convention Centre in Lagos on April 19. The victory also secured her the Miss International Nigeria 2026 title. Her pageant career includes winning Miss Grand Nigeria in 2022, after which she represented Nigeria at the Miss Grand International competition in Vietnam, where she reached the Top 20. She also represented Lagos State at the 2025 Miss Universe Nigeria pageant, finishing as first runner-up behind Onyinyechi Basil of Anambra State. Beyond pageantry, Bolarinde is a professional model, actress and entrepreneur. She is also the founder of The Unconventional Quest, an advocacy initiative that encourages young people to explore career paths outside conventional choices. Meanwhile, Elizaveta Kuznetsova of Moldova won the overall Miss International 2026 crown, becoming the first representative of her country to win the title.
